statements.text: Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.
Noah sent out a raven before he sent out a dove.
Noah planted a vineyard.
Noah had four sons who went into the ark with him.
statements.truth: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

statements.text: The ark came to rest on Mount Sinai.
statements.truth: The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

statements.text: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born.
Abraham's family set out from Ur of the Chaldeans.
Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah.
Abraham's son Ishmael was born to his wife Sarah.
statements.truth: Ishmael's mother was Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant.

statements.text: Abraham was 50 years old when he left Haran.
statements.truth: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

statements.text: Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a son.
Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
God changed Sarah's name from Sarai to Sarah.
Sarah was buried near Bethlehem.
statements.truth: Sarah was buried in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre at Hebron.

statements.text: Abraham said Sarah was 60 when God promised her a son.
statements.truth: Sarah was ninety when God promised her a son.

statements.text: Jacob worked seven years for Laban to marry Rachel.
Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching up to heaven.
Jacob was given the name Israel.
Jacob was born first, just before his twin brother Esau.
statements.truth: Esau was born first; Jacob came out grasping his heel.

statements.text: Jacob loved his wife Leah more than Rachel.
statements.truth: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah.

statements.text: Joseph's brothers sold him for twenty shekels of silver.
Joseph was thirty years old when he entered Pharaoh's service.
In prison, Joseph explained the dreams of a cupbearer and a baker.
Joseph was the firstborn of Jacob's twelve sons.
statements.truth: Reuben was Jacob's firstborn son.

statements.text: The traders took Joseph to Babylon after buying him from his brothers.
statements.truth: The traders took Joseph to Egypt.

statements.text: Moses was eighty years old when he spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses' father-in-law Jethro was a priest of Midian.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died.
As a baby, Moses was hidden in a basket by the Jordan River.
statements.truth: Moses' basket was placed among the reeds along the Nile.

statements.text: Moses led Israel across the Jordan into the promised land.
statements.truth: Moses saw the land from the mountain, but God told him he would not cross into it.

statements.text: Aaron was three years older than his brother Moses.
Aaron's staff sprouted, blossomed and produced almonds.
Aaron made a golden calf while Moses was on the mountain.
Aaron, the brother of Moses, belonged to the tribe of Judah.
statements.truth: Aaron was a Levite.

statements.text: Aaron's life came to an end on the top of Mount Sinai.
statements.truth: Aaron died on the top of Mount Hor.

statements.text: Miriam was called a prophetess.
Miriam led women in dancing with tambourines.
Miriam criticized Moses over his Cushite marriage.
Miriam was the aunt of Moses.
statements.truth: Miriam, Aaron and Moses were children of Amram and Jochebed.

statements.text: Miriam died in Egypt before the Exodus.
statements.truth: Miriam died and was buried at Kadesh, in the wilderness.

statements.text: Joshua was one of the twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
The wall of Jericho collapsed when the people shouted.
Joshua died at the age of 110.
Joshua was from the tribe of Levi.
statements.truth: Joshua son of Nun, then called Hoshea, was from the tribe of Ephraim.

statements.text: Israel marched around Jericho for forty days.
statements.truth: On the seventh day they marched around Jericho seven times.

statements.text: Rahab hid two Israelite spies on her roof.
Rahab let the spies down from her window by a rope.
Rahab is named in Matthew's family line of Jesus.
Rahab lived in the city of Ai.
statements.truth: Rahab lived in Jericho.

statements.text: Rahab hung a blue cloth from her window as a sign.
statements.truth: Rahab tied a scarlet cord in her window.

statements.text: Deborah held court under a palm tree.
Deborah was a prophetess who judged Israel.
Deborah and Barak sang a song together.
Deborah killed the enemy commander Sisera herself.
statements.truth: Jael, the wife of Heber, killed Sisera with a tent peg.

statements.text: Deborah's army commander was Gideon.
statements.truth: Deborah summoned Barak son of Abinoam to lead the army.

statements.text: Gideon tested God with a fleece of wool.
Gideon's army was cut down to three hundred men.
Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress when the angel came.
Gideon's family belonged to the tribe of Judah.
statements.truth: Gideon said his clan was the weakest in Manasseh.

statements.text: Gideon agreed to become Israel's king.
statements.truth: Gideon refused: he would not rule over Israel, for the LORD would rule.

statements.text: Samson tore apart a young lion with his bare hands.
Samson struck down a thousand men with a donkey's jawbone.
Samson tied torches to the tails of foxes.
Delilah handed Samson over to the Egyptians.
statements.truth: Delilah handed Samson over to the Philistines.

statements.text: Samson's family was from the tribe of Benjamin.
statements.truth: Samson's father Manoah was from the tribe of Dan.

statements.text: Ruth came from the land of Moab.
Ruth gathered grain in the field of Boaz.
Ruth was the great-grandmother of King David.
Ruth's mother-in-law was named Rachel.
statements.truth: Ruth's mother-in-law was Naomi.

statements.text: Ruth went back to Moab when Naomi left for Bethlehem.
statements.truth: Ruth refused to leave Naomi: "Wherever you go, I will go."

statements.text: Hannah prayed for a son at the house of the LORD in Shiloh.
Hannah brought Samuel to Eli.
Each year Hannah made Samuel a little robe.
Hannah's husband was named Jesse.
statements.truth: Hannah's husband was Elkanah.

statements.text: Hannah later had three more sons and three daughters.
statements.truth: Hannah later had three more sons and two daughters.

statements.text: As a boy, Samuel heard the LORD call his name in the night.
Samuel anointed Saul with a flask of oil.
Samuel anointed David, the youngest of Jesse's sons.
Samuel was serving Zadok when the LORD first called his name.
statements.truth: Samuel was ministering to the LORD before Eli when the LORD called him.

statements.text: Samuel's sons followed his ways as honest judges.
statements.truth: Samuel's sons did not walk in his ways; they took bribes.

statements.text: David was the youngest son of Jesse.
David played the harp to soothe King Saul.
David was thirty years old when he became king.
David chose seven stones before facing Goliath.
statements.truth: David chose five smooth stones from the brook.

statements.text: Jonathan, David's friend, was Samuel's son.
statements.truth: Jonathan was the son of Saul.

statements.text: Solomon asked God for an understanding heart.
Solomon finished building the temple.
Sheba's queen tested Solomon with difficult questions.
Solomon's mother was Michal.
statements.truth: Solomon's mother was Bathsheba.

statements.text: Solomon reigned over Israel for twenty years.
statements.truth: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.

statements.text: Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat by a brook.
Elijah faced the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elijah chose Gehazi to be the prophet after him.
statements.truth: God told Elijah to anoint Elisha son of Shaphat to succeed him.

statements.text: Elijah fled Jezebel and reached Egypt after forty days.
statements.truth: Elijah fled to Beersheba and on to Horeb, the mountain of God.

statements.text: Elisha asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.
Elisha made an iron axe head float.
Elisha told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan.
Elisha was the son of Amoz.
statements.truth: Elisha was the son of Shaphat.

statements.text: Elisha was mending fishing nets when Elijah called him.
statements.truth: Elisha was plowing with twelve teams of oxen when Elijah called him.

statements.text: Jonah boarded a ship bound for Tarshish.
Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
God made a plant grow up to shade Jonah's head.
God sent Jonah to preach to the city of Babylon.
statements.truth: God sent Jonah to the great city of Nineveh.

statements.text: The people of Nineveh ignored Jonah's warning.
statements.truth: The people of Nineveh believed God and proclaimed a fast.

statements.text: Esther was raised by her cousin Mordecai.
Esther became queen in place of Vashti.
Esther asked the Jews in Susa to fast for three days.
Esther was made queen by King Nebuchadnezzar.
statements.truth: King Xerxes made Esther queen.

statements.text: Esther's other name was Miriam.
statements.truth: Esther's other name was Hadassah.

statements.text: Daniel asked to be given vegetables to eat instead of the king's food.
Daniel prayed three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem.
Daniel read the writing on the wall for King Belshazzar.
King Nebuchadnezzar had Daniel thrown into the lions' den.
statements.truth: It was King Darius who had Daniel thrown into the lions' den.

statements.text: Daniel was taken away to Assyria as a young man.
statements.truth: Daniel was among the young men taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.

statements.text: Nehemiah was cupbearer to the king.
Nehemiah's builders worked with a weapon in one hand.
The wall was completed in fifty-two days.
Nehemiah served wine to King Nebuchadnezzar.
statements.truth: Nehemiah served King Artaxerxes.

statements.text: Nehemiah was the priest who read the Law aloud to the people.
statements.truth: Ezra the priest read the Law to the people; Nehemiah was the governor.

statements.text: The angel Gabriel told Mary she would have a son.
Mary went to visit her relative Elizabeth.
Mary stood near the cross when Jesus was crucified.
Mary was living in Bethlehem when the angel came to her.
statements.truth: Gabriel was sent to Mary in Nazareth, a town in Galilee.

statements.text: Mary was engaged to a man named Zechariah.
statements.truth: Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, of the house of David.

statements.text: John the Baptist ate locusts and wild honey.
John's father Zechariah was a priest.
John the Baptist was beheaded on Herod's orders.
John the Baptist wore fine robes of linen.
statements.truth: John wore clothing of camel's hair with a leather belt.

statements.text: John baptized the Jerusalem crowds in the Sea of Galilee.
statements.truth: John baptized those crowds in the Jordan River.

statements.text: Peter walked on the water toward Jesus.
Peter denied knowing Jesus three times.
Peter's brother was Andrew.
Peter was collecting taxes when Jesus called him.
statements.truth: Peter was a fisherman, casting a net into the sea.

statements.text: Jesus gave Peter the name Matthew.
statements.truth: Jesus said Simon would be called Cephas, which is translated as Peter.

statements.text: Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus.
Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector in Jericho.
Zacchaeus promised to give half his possessions to the poor.
Zacchaeus was so tall he could see over the crowd.
statements.truth: Zacchaeus was small in stature and could not see over the crowd.

statements.text: Zacchaeus promised to pay back twice what he had cheated.
statements.truth: Zacchaeus promised to repay anyone he had cheated fourfold.

statements.text: Paul was born in Tarsus.
Paul was blinded by a light on the road to Damascus.
Paul was shipwrecked on the island of Malta.
Paul worked with Aquila and Priscilla as a fisherman.
statements.truth: Paul worked with them as a tentmaker.

statements.text: Paul was from the tribe of Judah.
statements.truth: Paul was from the tribe of Benjamin.

statements.text: Lydia was a dealer in purple cloth.
Lydia came from the city of Thyatira.
Lydia met Paul at a place of prayer by a river.
Paul spoke to Lydia at the riverside in Corinth.
statements.truth: Paul met Lydia at Philippi.

statements.text: Lydia came from the city of Athens.
statements.truth: Lydia came from Thyatira.
